PLAN REVIEW — PARALLEL DEPARTMENT REVIEW.
Continues _design/plan-review-reasoner: same product, same finding numbers, same three real citations.
Parallel review is the category's hardest-sold feature and the reasoner design pinned it. This is the argument.
SOURCE: P:\plan-review now declares DEPARTMENT_ROLES in src/staff-identity.mjs — the same seven roles proposed here — with personas orgId/userId holding roles reviewer/observer/applicant/staff. Re-read at origin/main 99c156ba on 2026-09-18; routing, discipline and sign-off still return nothing.
FIXTURE throughout.

THIS DESIGN NEEDS A RULING AMENDED, AND SAYS SO RATHER THAN ROUTING AROUND IT.
_decisions/2026-09-14_staff_identity_and_department_rbac.md gates PLAN REVIEW to Development services and city-manager. Parallel review requires Fire, Public works and Parks to reach it. As ruled, this cannot be built.
Proposed amendment, using that ruling's OWN logic: a department reaches plan review only through its own scope — its findings, its coverage, its sign-off. That is exactly what the ruling says makes Overview "a roll-up rather than a leak".
The roster stays the nine lenses. No new department is invented.

WE DO NOT ROUTE. WE SCOPE.
Which departments get a submittal is the city's decision and its workflow system's job — we said we are a companion and this is where that has teeth.
What a finding BELONGS to is decided by the section it cites, through a map the city declares once. Declared, so it is auditable and consistent; not inferred per submittal.
A section absent from the map does NOT default to Development services. It produces an unrouted finding.

UNROUTED HAS TWO CAUSES AND THEY ARE NOT THE SAME.
ZERO departments claim the section, or TWO do. Both are refusals to guess, and the surface never collapses them into one grey state.
This is the same shape as the absence taxonomy on the reasoner canvas: the reason for an absence is the product, not the absence itself.

COVERAGE IS PER DEPARTMENT, BECAUSE A GAP IS NOT SHARED.
Development services has four cited rules here. Public works has ZERO — nothing in our corpus reaches them, and the product says that to their face rather than implying coverage.
One coverage number across the application would let a strong department's corpus hide a weak one's gap. That is the single most dangerous number this product could print.

THE BOARD IS ABOUT THE APPLICATION, NEVER THE PEOPLE.
It shows where work is sitting and for how long. It does not rank staff, count individual throughput, or name who has not opened something. Handing a government customer a productivity leaderboard is a different product with a different politics, and we are not shipping it by accident.
THREE STATES THAT LOOK ALIKE: not opened / reviewed and found nothing / we produce nothing for them. Parks is the last two at once. Collapsing any of them is how a cycle closes on a review nobody did.

TWO DEPARTMENTS ARE TWO AUTHORITIES — the rule already exists.
Uncertain was reserved for two code editions disagreeing. A department disagreeing with a department is the same shape: name both, pick neither, escalate to the role that sees across lanes.
THE REFUSALS ARE THE DESIGN. Not the stricter number — stricter is not a synonym for correct, and it teaches every department that claiming higher wins. Not the claim that has a citation — our corpus is not an authority on which department governs the right of way. Not both numbers to the applicant.

ONE NOTICE, FOUR DEPARTMENTS, AND IT WILL NOT ISSUE.
The applicant gets one list, each item carrying its department beside its citation. Escalations print under a heading that says no action is required from them.
"Not evaluated" is broken out BY DEPARTMENT, and it states plainly that Public works has no rule in our corpus, so nothing in the notice reflects an automated check of their requirements.
The Issue button is not live while two departments have not opened the submittal. 8 + 2 + 2 + 0 + 1 = 13.

WHAT DOES NOT EXIST.
• No routing, no sign-off, no cycle, no declared section-to-department map — and the roster left this list: src/staff-identity.mjs declares DEPARTMENT_ROLES, the same seven roles proposed here. Everything else on this canvas is proposed.
• The ruling amendment above is a precondition, not a detail.
• Department colour is a SECOND CHANNEL (a dot) and determination stays the badge. One element never carries both.
• Still pinned from the reasoner canvas: the viewer, the dimension capture, and every adjudicator except the front setback.
